history.summary: Palm Gardens 3BR, 1,206 sqft at $1,288,000 ($1,068 psf) — a Keppel Land 694-unit 99LH (lease from 1996, 70 yrs left) in deep Choa Chu Kang, 220m to Keat Hong LRT. The algo's 801/1000 and its -16.2% 'age-adjusted district discount' do not survive verification: against the project's OWN URA prints the ask is at market, not below it. Last 12 months, 11 same-size (1,150-1,300 sqft) resales printed a median of $1,280,000 / $1,062 psf — this ask is +0.6% above that, and above the median of every floor band except 16-20. The discount is to the DISTRICT, and it is structural and not closing: Palm Gardens' 3BR band went $1,045 psf (2023) -> $1,060 (2024) -> $1,056 (2025) -> $1,062 (2026), i.e. ~+0.5%/yr, while D23's same-size 99LH resale stock went $1,110 -> $1,126 -> $1,182 -> $1,172 over the identical window. The project has been flat for three years AND has lagged its own district. Entry is honest and liquidity is genuinely deep, but for a 5-7yr resale-profit mandate there is no edge here at $1.288M — it is OCR beta with a 1996 lease clock, bought at full price against ~10-16 near-identical 1,206 sqft 3BRs listed in the same project right now.
history.rating_rationale: VERIFY-FIRST APPLIED, DISCOUNT DID NOT SURVIVE. The MMR 801 is carried by two components — age_value +12.11 and appreciation +7.1 — and both fail verification. (1) age_value credits a -16.2% premium_vs_age_adjusted_median vs the D23 size band. But psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct is +1.2% (above the project's own median), and the project's own 138 URA prints confirm it: 38 prints in the 1,150-1,300 sqft band since Feb-24 median $1,280,000 / $1,060 psf; the 11 prints in the last 12 months median $1,280,000 / $1,062 psf; 2026 YTD $1,286,000. The $1,288,000 ask is AT market. The gap to the district is a persistent location/vintage discount (Palm Gardens $1,062 vs D23 same-band 99LH $1,172 = -9.4%), sitting mid-pack against its true CCK peer set (Regent Grove $1,003, Northvale $1,107, Regent Heights $1,132, Parkview $972). It is priced correctly for what it is, not mispriced. (2) The 6.37%/yr ura_5yr_cagr is entirely the 2021-23 post-COVID catch-up ($780 -> $1,045 psf); since 2023 the 3BR band has done ~+0.5%/yr. momentum is already flagged -1.0 (worst reading), and per repo priors trailing CAGR has ~zero forward power anyway. The 6.35%/yr ROI projection should not be relied on — override set to 2.5%/yr (OCR baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the demonstrated 3-year district lag and a 1996 lease clock). At 2.5% the 5yr all-cash outcome is roughly +1.5%/yr capital plus ~2.1% net yield after $39.6k entry costs and exit commission — a poor return on $1.29M of locked capital for a profit-seeking mandate. WHY NOT AVOID: nothing here is broken or overpriced. Entry is honest, liquidity is real (138 URA txns across 694 units, deep buyer_pool, ~18-20 same-band resales a year), Keppel Land build with private lift lobbies and full facilities (bowling alley, tennis) that reviews consistently rate well-maintained, quantum is $500k inside the $1.8M budget, OCR is the favoured forward region, and Choa Chu Kang becomes an NSL x Jurong Region Line interchange in mid-2028 — a dated catalyst inside the hold window, 826m away. WHY NOT BUY: he would be paying full price for three years of zero appreciation in a project that underperforms its own district, competing at exit against a large stack of undifferentiated clones. This only becomes a Buy on a negotiated entry: at ~$1.20-1.22M (a real 5-6% below the project's own 12-month median, achievable given how many sellers are cutting) the margin of safety would carry the lease decay and the thesis flips.
red_flags: NO DISCOUNT vs the project's own comps — ask $1,288,000 is +0.6% above the trailing-12mo median print ($1,280,000, n=11) and +1.2% above the URA project median; the algo's -16.2% 'cheapness' is a district comparison, not unit value

THREE YEARS FLAT — Palm Gardens 3BR band median: $1,260k (2023) / $1,280k (2024) / $1,277.5k (2025) / $1,286k (2026) ≈ +0.5%/yr; the 6.37% headline CAGR is all 2021-23 catch-up and momentum is flagged -1.0

UNDERPERFORMS ITS OWN DISTRICT — D23 same-size 99LH resale psf rose $1,110 -> $1,172 (2023-26, +5.6%) while Palm Gardens rose $1,045 -> $1,062 (+1.6%); the structural discount is widening, not converging

HEAVY SAME-TYPE COMPETITION — ~10-16 near-identical 1,206/1,216 sqft 3BRs listed concurrently in the same 694-unit project (blocks 2A/2B/2C/2D/2E/3 Hong San Walk) asking $1.288M-$1.40M, most with recent price cuts; that is ~8-10 months of inventory against ~18-20 band resales/yr, and it is the same wall he must sell into in 5-7 years
LEASE FROM 1996 — 70 yrs left today, 63-65 at exit; an older clock than most D23 peers, and the decay is very likely part of why the project has stalled while the district moved

catalysts: Choa Chu Kang becomes an NSL x Jurong Region Line interchange — JRL Stage 1 (CCK-Boon Lay/Tawas) now mid-2028 after a six-month LTA delay; a genuine dated catalyst 826m away, inside a 5-7yr hold
Genuinely deep liquidity — 138 URA transactions, 694 units, ~18-20 same-band resales a year and a deep HDB-upgrader pool in Choa Chu Kang; exit is slow-priced but never stuck

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: $3,800/mo from ura_project_bed (confidence 0.95) = 3.54% gross / 2.11% net. Sits mid-range against EdgeProp's quoted $2.10-$3.90 psf/mo for the project ($3.15 psf here). Credible and not an artifact — no >5.5% yield flag. But this is carry only: the repo's own backtest finds high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_β -0.16), and 2.11% net does not compensate for a project appreciating at ~0.5%/yr.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 6.37%/yr ura_5yr_cagr (138 txns, data_confidence 1.0) is arithmetically real but structurally misleading — it is the 2021-23 recovery ($780 -> $1,011 -> $1,045 psf) with a three-year plateau bolted on the end. Project 3BR-band medians: 2023 $1,045 psf / $1,260k, 2024 $1,060 / $1,280k, 2025 $1,056 / $1,277.5k, 2026 YTD $1,062 / $1,286k. Over the same window D23's same-size 99LH stock ran $1,110 -> $1,126 -> $1,182 -> $1,172, so the project lagged its district by ~4pp cumulative. momentum is already -1.0. Override to 2.5%/yr on resale-to-resale URA evidence: OCR baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the demonstrated lag and the 1996 lease clock. Do not underwrite this at 6.37%.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for Palm Gardens (stack_profile.status = not_researched) and floor_level/facing are 0% populated in this DB, so the unit's stack, floor and outlook are unknown — this is a stated data gap, not an assumption of a good or bad floor. What can be said from URA floor bands (1,150-1,300 sqft, since Feb-24): 01-05 median $1,255k (n=9, $1.100-1.315M), 06-10 $1,260k (n=8), 11-15 $1,280k (n=15), 16-20 $1,299k (n=6). The floor premium is modest (~3.5% low-to-high), so floor uncertainty is less damaging here than usual — but it does mean $1,288,000 is above the median of every band except 16-20. Worth running /research-development before any offer, and worth asking the agent for the exact floor: a 03-floor unit at this ask is straightforwardly overpaying.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale URA prints only (data/ura_district_D23.csv, 138 Palm Gardens rows). Project 3BR-band (1,150-1,300 sqft) medians 2023 $1,260k -> 2026 YTD $1,286k = ~+0.7%/yr; D23 same-size 99LH resale $1,110 -> $1,172 psf = ~+1.8%/yr over the same window. Set at 2.5%/yr = OCR regional baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the project's measured 3-year lag vs its district and accelerating decay on a 1996 lease. No portal headline CAGR used.

history.summary: A 1,216 sqft unit at Palm Gardens (Keppel Land, 694 units, 99LH from Aug-1996, D23 Choa Chu Kang) asking $1,260,000 / $1,036 psf. It is advertised as a 4BR but it is not one: Palm Gardens' true 4BRs are 1,346/1,432/2,336 sqft and print $1.41M-$1.65M, while 1,206/1,216 sqft is the project's dominant 3BR product (95 of 138 URA prints). Priced correctly as a 3BR, the ask is at market, not below it, and the 5-7yr resale-profit case does not clear entry costs.
history.rating_rationale: Three verified, independent problems. (1) THE BED COUNT IS WRONG. URA rental filings put Palm Gardens 4BRs at 1,350-2,350 sqft (median 1,450, n=28) and 3BRs at ~1,250 sqft (n=160); 1,216 sqft sits below the 4BR floor and inside the 3BR band. Six other 1,216 sqft Palm Gardens listings in the DB are all labelled 3BR - only this one says 4BR. 99.co/PropertyGuru project data independently states Palm Gardens 3BRs run 1,206-1,744 sqft. bed_bands returns 'ok' only because the 12% tolerance covers the gap; the evidence is unambiguous. A buyer shortlisting 'a 4BR at $1.26M' is being shown a 3BR - real 4BRs there cost $1.41M-$1.65M. (2) THERE IS NO DISCOUNT. Against the project's own 24-month prints for the 1,190-1,230 sqft band - 32 resales, median $1,277,500 / $1,055 psf - this ask is only ~1.5% below, and ~2.5% below the 2026 median ($1,292,000). The algo's -18.7% 'age-adjusted district discount' is a comparison to a wider 1,050-1,400 sqft cross-project band, not to this unit's own comps; Palm Gardens' ~9% level discount to D23 peers has been stable since 2023 (-8.4% then, -9.4% now) - a permanent location level, not a closing gap. (3) THE SEGMENT HAS STALLED. Palm Gardens' 1,206/1,216 band: $1,028 psf (2023) -> $1,062 (2026), ~+1.1%/yr; D23 same-size 99LH peers excluding Palm Gardens: $1,122 -> $1,172, ~+1.5%/yr - and 2026 medians are BELOW 2025 on both. The headline 6.37% CAGR is entirely 2021-23 post-COVID catch-up (momentum flagged -1.0). At a defensible 2.0%/yr the all-cash ROI is 2.6%/yr over 5 years, below risk-free, and at the peer group's realized 1.5%/yr the ~$38.5k BSD is barely recovered. Add ~18 near-identical 1,205-1,216 sqft 3BRs listed in this one project right now against ~16 band resales a year - over a year of standing inventory, and the same wall at exit. The 823/1000 is the highest of all 22 Palm Gardens listings for one reason: it carries the lowest ask in the band ($1.26M vs $1.288M next cheapest), a ~2% gap the model reads as value. Finally, this listing was seen exactly once, on 2026-06-08, and has not reappeared in 51 days while 15 sibling Palm Gardens listings polled on 2026-07-28 - it is very likely sold or withdrawn. To be clear, this is a listing-level Avoid, not a claim the project is uninvestable: realsmart's 81.3% profitable on 862 resales is real downside evidence, and if this unit were live and honestly described as a 3BR at $1.26M it would be a Neutral - marginally the best-priced of eighteen.
red_flags: MISLABELLED BEDROOM COUNT - advertised 4BR at 1,216 sqft, but URA rental bands (4BR 1,350-2,350 sqft median 1,450, n=28 vs 3BR ~1,250 sqft, n=160), six sibling 1,216 sqft listings all labelled 3BR, and 99.co project data (3BR = 1,206-1,744 sqft) all say this is a 3BR; true Palm Gardens 4BRs (1,346/1,432 sqft) print $1.41M-$1.65M

NO DISCOUNT vs its own comps - $1,036 psf against a 24mo band median of $1,055 psf / $1,277,500 (n=32) is ~1.5% below, and ~2.5% below the 2026 median $1,292,000; the algo's -18.7% is a cross-project size-band artifact
LISTING LIKELY DEAD - first_seen = last_seen = 2026-06-08, times_seen = 1, no reappearance in 51 days while 15 sibling Palm Gardens listings polled 2026-07-28

SEGMENT FLAT AND ROLLING OVER - Palm Gardens 1206/1216 band +1.1%/yr since 2023, D23 same-size 99LH peers (ex-Palm Gardens) +1.5%/yr, and BOTH 2026 medians are below 2025 ($1,182->$1,159 incl PG; $1,226->$1,172 excl)
STALE TRAILING CAGR - the 6.37% ura_5yr_cagr is all 2021-23 catch-up ($780 psf -> $1,028); the last three years are ~+1.1%/yr and momentum is flagged -1.0

SUPPLY WALL - ~18 near-identical 1,205-1,216 sqft 3BRs listed concurrently in this one 694-unit project asking $1.288M-$1.400M, against ~16 same-band resales/yr; that is >1 year of inventory and the identical wall he must sell into in 5-7 years

PERSISTENT, NON-CONVERGING DISCOUNT - Palm Gardens trades ~9% under D23 same-size 99LH peers and has since 2023 (-8.4% -> -9.4%); this is a structural location level that inflates age_value, not a dislocation that closes
LEASE FROM 12-AUG-1996 - 70 years left today, ~63 at a 5-7yr exit; decay accelerates as the 60-year CPF/financing thresholds approach
THIN CARRY - $3,900/mo on 5 URA contracts = 3.71% gross, 2.08% net; does not compensate for flat capital, and at 2.0%/yr appreciation the 5yr all-cash ROI is 2.6%/yr, below risk-free

NO FLOOR, FACING OR STACK DATA - floor_level and facing are unpopulated for this record and there is no researched profile, so the unit cannot be placed; URA floor bands spread ~$1,238k (low) to ~$1,322k (high) within this size, a ~7% range the ask cannot be checked against
very_old_property (26 years) and very_low_psf flags both fire; the low PSF is the region/project level effect, not condition-driven value
catalysts: Genuinely deep exit liquidity - 1,558 lifetime transactions, 862 resales, 694 units, ~16 same-band resales/yr and a 71%-HDB-buyer pool (realsmart); pricing is slow but a seller is never stuck

Strong downside record - realsmart REALSCORE 3.9/5 with 81.3% of 862 resales sold at a profit (698 profitable / 164 not), avg holding 9.1 yrs, avg annualized 4.7%; deep enough to be real evidence that owners here rarely lose money - backward-looking, not a forward forecast

OCR is the backtested-favoured forward region (+3.7%/yr realized vs RCR +3.1, CCR +1.9)

agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Three verified, independent problems. (1) THE BED COUNT IS WRONG. URA rental filings put Palm Gardens 4BRs at 1,350-2,350 sqft (median 1,450, n=28) and 3BRs at ~1,250 sqft (n=160); 1,216 sqft sits below the 4BR floor and inside the 3BR band. Six other 1,216 sqft Palm Gardens listings in the DB are all labelled 3BR - only this one says 4BR. 99.co/PropertyGuru project data independently states Palm Gardens 3BRs run 1,206-1,744 sqft. bed_bands returns 'ok' only because the 12% tolerance covers the gap; the evidence is unambiguous. A buyer shortlisting 'a 4BR at $1.26M' is being shown a 3BR - real 4BRs there cost $1.41M-$1.65M. (2) THERE IS NO DISCOUNT. Against the project's own 24-month prints for the 1,190-1,230 sqft band - 32 resales, median $1,277,500 / $1,055 psf - this ask is only ~1.5% below, and ~2.5% below the 2026 median ($1,292,000). The algo's -18.7% 'age-adjusted district discount' is a comparison to a wider 1,050-1,400 sqft cross-project band, not to this unit's own comps; Palm Gardens' ~9% level discount to D23 peers has been stable since 2023 (-8.4% then, -9.4% now) - a permanent location level, not a closing gap. (3) THE SEGMENT HAS STALLED. Palm Gardens' 1,206/1,216 band: $1,028 psf (2023) -> $1,062 (2026), ~+1.1%/yr; D23 same-size 99LH peers excluding Palm Gardens: $1,122 -> $1,172, ~+1.5%/yr - and 2026 medians are BELOW 2025 on both. The headline 6.37% CAGR is entirely 2021-23 post-COVID catch-up (momentum flagged -1.0). At a defensible 2.0%/yr the all-cash ROI is 2.6%/yr over 5 years, below risk-free, and at the peer group's realized 1.5%/yr the ~$38.5k BSD is barely recovered. Add ~18 near-identical 1,205-1,216 sqft 3BRs listed in this one project right now against ~16 band resales a year - over a year of standing inventory, and the same wall at exit. The 823/1000 is the highest of all 22 Palm Gardens listings for one reason: it carries the lowest ask in the band ($1.26M vs $1.288M next cheapest), a ~2% gap the model reads as value. Finally, this listing was seen exactly once, on 2026-06-08, and has not reappeared in 51 days while 15 sibling Palm Gardens listings polled on 2026-07-28 - it is very likely sold or withdrawn. To be clear, this is a listing-level Avoid, not a claim the project is uninvestable: realsmart's 81.3% profitable on 862 resales is real downside evidence, and if this unit were live and honestly described as a 3BR at $1.26M it would be a Neutral - marginally the best-priced of eighteen.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Modest and well-evidenced but thin. $3,900/mo comes from 5 URA project-bedroom contracts over 12 months (confidence 0.71) - a real number, not a model guess. That is 3.71% gross / 2.08% net on the ask. Tenant demand in Choa Chu Kang is steady but price-capped: the catchment is HDB-upgrader and west-industrial rather than expat, and Tengah's new-town build-out adds competing stock. Carry covers holding costs with little left over; it cannot rescue a flat capital thesis.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 6.37% ura_5yr_cagr is not a forward number - it is entirely the 2021-23 post-COVID OCR repricing ($780 -> $1,028 psf in two years), after which the band has done ~+1.1%/yr. Critically, this is NOT a Palm-Gardens-specific failure: D23 same-size 99LH peers excluding Palm Gardens managed only ~+1.5%/yr over the same three years, and both series printed 2026 medians below 2025. The whole D23 large-format 99LH resale segment has stalled and is rolling over. Palm Gardens' ~9% discount to those peers is stable and structural, so there is no convergence trade either. Against the OCR baseline of +3.7%/yr I mark this down heavily for the stalled segment, the 70-year lease and the standing inventory, and use 2.0%/yr - at which the all-cash 5yr ROI is 2.6%/yr. Confidence is medium, not high: the model explains <10% of forward variance and 2026 is a partial year (n=47 in the peer set), so the rollover could be mix or noise.
